# Toph

Toph is a self-hosted workbench for a homelab. It runs on your server and provides a browser client and an Android APK.

## Core facts

- Single-tenant, self-hosted, MIT licensed.
- Go backend with embedded React web client.
- Android client: Kotlin/Jetpack Compose.
- Tabs: code editor, database console, OpenCode AI chat, terminal, web app.
- Browser editor: Monaco.
- Android editor: CodeMirror 6 in a local WebView.
- Web app tabs: Android WebView; browser iframe with external fallback.
- The server owns files, PTYs, database credentials and AI sessions.
- Clients are thin and connect over HTTPS/WSS.
- Not a VS Code fork, not a multi-tenant SaaS, not a complete DBeaver replacement.

## Architecture

Browser (React) and Android (Compose) connect to the Go server over HTTPS/WSS.

The Go server provides:
- authentication and sessions;
- projects and workspace files;
- ripgrep search and git status;
- PTY terminals;
- SQL and NoSQL database gateway;
- OpenCode proxy;
- web target registry;
- embedded web build.

Repositories, databases and OpenCode remain on the server. Database credentials are encrypted with AES-GCM and never sent to clients.

## Install

One command (Debian/Ubuntu/LXC):

    curl -fsSL https://github.com/ferforastieri/toph/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sudo sh

Docker:

    git clone https://github.com/ferforastieri/toph.git
    cd toph
    TOPH_WORKSPACES_HOST=/srv/workspaces \
    TOPH_ADMIN_PASSWORD='strong-password' \
    docker compose -f deploy/compose.yaml up --build

Binary:

    make build
    TOPH_WORKSPACES=/srv/workspaces \
    TOPH_ADMIN_PASSWORD='strong-password' \
    ./bin/toph

Open:

    http://127.0.0.1:8787/

Landing page: `/`
Application: `/app`
Docs: `/docs.html`
Machine-readable docs: `/llms.txt`

## Android

Download the signed APK from GitHub Releases. Debug APKs are not published.

Local development only:

    cd android
    ./gradlew assembleDebug

On first launch, enter the Toph server URL, username and password. Use LAN, VPN or Tailscale. Do not expose Toph directly to the internet.

## Configuration

TOPH_ADDR=127.0.0.1:8787
TOPH_DATA_DIR=./data
TOPH_WORKSPACES=/workspaces
TOPH_ADMIN_PASSWORD=
TOPH_SECURE_COOKIES=false
TOPH_OPENCODE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3005
TOPH_OPENCODE_AUTH=
TOPH_BUILD_ID=
TOPH_WEB_DIR=

TOPH_WORKSPACES is a colon-separated list of existing directories. Projects must be inside these roots.

TOPH_OPENCODE_AUTH is a raw Authorization header sent by the server-side OpenCode proxy.

## Databases

SQL/CQL drivers: PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, SQLite, SQL Server, Oracle, ClickHouse, Cassandra. Search/graph: Elasticsearch, Neo4j.

DSN examples:

    PostgreSQL   postgres://user:pass@host:5432/db?sslmode=disable
    MySQL        user:pass@tcp(host:3306)/db
    SQLite       /path/to/database.db
    SQL Server   sqlserver://user:pass@host:1433?database=db
    Oracle       oracle://user:pass@host:1521/service
    ClickHouse   clickhouse://user:pass@host:9000/db

MongoDB query format:

    {"database":"app","collection":"users","filter":{},"limit":100}

MongoDB aggregation uses `pipeline` instead of `filter`.

Redis query format: a Redis command string.

    GET session:42
    HGETALL user:1
    SCAN 0 COUNT 100

Read-only profiles reject writes. SQL profiles use read-only drivers/queries where supported.

SQL table tabs support row editing when the table has a primary key and the profile is not read-only. Updates use the primary key in the WHERE clause.

Cassandra uses CQL. Elasticsearch accepts JSON `{index, body}`. Neo4j accepts Cypher.

## OpenCode

Toph proxies the OpenCode V2 HTTP API. Chat is native in both clients. Sessions use the project root as the OpenCode location. Tool permission requests can be allowed once, always, or rejected.

The server must be able to reach OpenCode. Set TOPH_OPENCODE_URL and, when required, TOPH_OPENCODE_AUTH.

## Updates

Web: polls `/api/version`. When `buildId` changes, a toast appears; clicking reloads and clears caches.

Android: checks the latest GitHub release for an APK. When a newer tag exists with an APK asset, a toast appears; clicking downloads the APK and opens the Android installer. Android requires the final install confirmation. Release builds use a signing keystore when the Android secrets are configured; otherwise the workflow publishes a debug APK.

## Security

- Bind to localhost, LAN or VPN.
- Put TLS in front.
- Use a strong password.
- Login is rate-limited.
- Session tokens are opaque and stored hashed.
- Project paths are restricted with symlink escape checks.
- Database credentials are encrypted at rest.
- Treat Toph as remote administration.

## API summary

GET  /api/health
GET  /api/version
POST /api/auth/login
GET  /api/auth/me
POST /api/auth/logout
GET  /api/projects
POST /api/projects
GET  /api/projects/:id/tree
GET  /api/projects/:id/file
PUT  /api/projects/:id/file
POST /api/projects/:id/search
GET  /api/projects/:id/git/status
POST /api/projects/:id/terminals
GET  /api/terminals/:id/ws
GET  /api/db/profiles
POST /api/db/profiles
POST /api/db/profiles/:id/query
GET  /api/db/profiles/:id/schema
GET  /api/web-targets
POST /api/web-targets
ALL  /api/opencode/*

## Development

    go test ./...
    go vet ./...

    cd web
    npm test
    npm run build

    cd ../android
    ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest assembleDebug
